scenario.preconditions: Haxe 4.3.7, Reflaxe 4.0.0-beta, exact php74-modern-v1, and native PHP 8.4.7
scenario.input: the existing ordinary-Haxe tracer plus the two-module semantics.Main -> semantics.Calculator differential fixture
scenario.actionOrCompilationPath: authored Haxe -> Reflaxe callbacks in arbitrary order -> source-derived typed dependency plan -> one mapped PHP artifact per owned type -> separate mapped bootstrap -> staged ownership -> downstream WordPress package builder -> extracted PHP runtime
scenario.observableResult: collision-safe per-type paths and maps are deterministic, Calculator loads before Main, bootstrap invokes the Haxe-selected main, and PHP copied from the deterministic WordPress-owned ZIP prints the manually authored tracer result with empty stderr
scenario.errorOrEdgeBehavior: missing or floating profiles, missing/cyclic dependencies, path collisions, stale or modified owned files, unowned collisions, malformed ledgers, stale package digests, and unsupported AST publish no accepted output
scenario.protectedClaim: per-type artifact identity/path, source-derived dependency order, explicit php74-modern-v1 policy, exact per-file maps, same-process staged ownership/rollback, and one-way deterministic WordPress packaging only; namespaces, general autoloading, cross-process crash recovery, broad modern-PHP syntax, WordPress runtime compatibility, official Haxe qualification, publication, and production support remain unclaimed

redState.command: cd compiler/reflaxe.php && haxe test/semantic-matrix/build.hxml; test -f build/semantic-matrix/bootstrap.php
redState.failure: the compiler emitted only _GeneratedFiles.json, main.php, and main.php.haxe-map.json; bootstrap.php did not exist
redState.reason: the tracer still used Reflaxe's monolithic output shape and did not own a module graph or separate entry artifact

independentOracle: stock Haxe 4.3.7 execution of the same authored fixtures
manually reviewed per-type PHP, bootstrap.php, and expected stdout
independent Python verification of source spans, paths, graph edges, hashes, and ownership records
native PHP parser/runtime observation of both the build graph and PHP extracted from the WordPress-owned ZIP
byte-identical clean rebuild and package invariants

questions: Can Reflaxe callback order alter the graph, paths, or bootstrap?
Are dependencies derived from typed source rather than hand-authored package metadata?
Can an unowned or locally modified file be overwritten or removed?
Can a failed compilation or package validation publish a partial accepted artifact?
Do any maps, manifests, diagnostics, or ZIP entries contain machine-local paths?
Does the WordPress package proof overstate real WordPress runtime compatibility?
findingsAndDispositions: Reflaxe's generic output cleanup was incompatible with exact ownership; disabled it and made the compiler publish through a content-bound manifest-last owner.
A basename-only module path could collide; replaced it with length-prefixed module and type segments plus duplicate identity/path rejection.
Compiler callback order could not define include order; collected typed static references and topologically ordered the complete graph after lowering.
A floating PHP target would make syntax policy implicit; required the exact php74-modern-v1 profile and added missing/unknown profile negatives.

The first WordPress consumer design could have confused package boot with WordPress compatibility; the package manifest explicitly records wordpressRuntimeCompatibility as not-claimed and the test does not enter the WordPress runtime scorecard.
Cross-process crash journaling, symlink-component confinement, namespaces, and autoloaders are not established by this slice and remain outside the protected claim.
